affiliations.date_precision: The obituary says Baker practiced general law in Washington from the mid-1930s, but it does not name a firm, define the employment relationship, or give an exact start date.
affiliations.research_notes: This is an occupation-only affiliation. No firm is named, the practice is not presumed to be self-employment, and it is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant (Junior Grade) Gibbs L. Baker is very likely Washington lawyer Gibbs Latimer Baker, a World War II Navy veteran documented in 1943 OSS Africa correspondence.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Gibbs L. Baker to Harris, Pouch Letter #3, 24 September 1943
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A peer-reviewed study cites two 1943 OSS documents naming Gibbs L. Baker and expands the initials GB as Gibbs Baker; a reputable obituary identifies Gibbs Latimer Baker as a World War II Navy veteran.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact first name, matching middle initial, commissioned naval status, World War II Navy service, and independently cited 1943 OSS correspondence. The index's private identifier has not yet been matched to a second official record.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly source places Gibbs L. Baker in OSS correspondence in September and November 1943; the obituary independently establishes World War II Navy service.
claims.match_notes: This is not marked confirmed because the physical personnel file and a second official record carrying the same private identifier have not been reviewed. The older Gibbs Latimer Baker in a 1910 directory is a different generation and is explicitly rejected.

claims.claim_text: Gibbs Latimer Baker practiced general law in Washington from the mid-1930s, before his World War II Navy and OSS service.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary dates Baker's Washington law practice from the mid-1930s and separately identifies him as a World War II Navy veteran; 1943 OSS correspondence establishes the wartime context.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the rare exact name, matching middle initial, indexed LT JG rank, obituary's World War II Navy service, and the scholarly source's 1943 OSS correspondence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation beginning in the mid-1930s. The obituary does not establish that law practice was the immediate predecessor to Navy or OSS service.
claims.match_notes: No firm is named, so no employer or self-employment relationship is inferred. The older Gibbs Latimer Baker's 1910 firm is not assigned to this person.
